artists.biography: Knifeworld is the new band from Kavus Torabi (Cardiacs, The Monsoon Bassoon, Guapo). The forthcoming album also features a handful of special guests, including Ben Jacobs (Max Tundra) on trumpet, Melanie Woods (Sidi Bou Said, Cardiacs) on vocals, Katharine Blake (Miranda Sex Garden, Mediæval Bæbes) on recorders, Sarah Measures (The Monsoon Bassoon, Mothlite) on horns and flute, and Khyam Allami on drums. Pissed Up On Brake Fluid, the first Knifeworld single, will be released by Believers Roast on July 13th 2009. It is probably the closest thing to a 'straightforward rock song' Torabi has ever written. The B-side, Happy Half-life, Dear Friend is not. It's barely even rock. It is, however, extremely psychedelic. Forthcoming debut album, Buried Alone: Tales Of Crushing Defeat, is a sprawling psychedelic meisterwork, taking in elements of pop, heavy rock, hardcore, avant-progressive and folk, and is due out on August 10th 2009. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Home of the Newly Departed" is the second studio album by British rock band Knifeworld, originally released in 2015 on Believers Roast. The album is a vibrant blend of progressive rock and art rock, characterized by intricate arrangements, dynamic shifts, and a kaleidoscopic use of instrumentation. Knifeworld, led by Kavus Torabi, crafts a sound that is both adventurous and melodic, drawing on influences from psychedelic rock, jazz, and avant-garde music. The album features complex vocal harmonies, layered guitars, and a rich tapestry of keyboards and woodwinds, creating a distinctive sonic identity within the modern rock landscape.

In Knifeworld's discography, "Home of the Newly Departed" marks a significant evolution from their earlier work, showcasing a more refined and ambitious approach to songwriting and production. It follows their debut album "Buried Alone: Tales of Crushing Defeat" (2009) and solidifies the band's reputation for pushing the boundaries of rock music. The album received positive critical attention for its creativity and musicianship, earning a rating of 3.20 on Prog Archives based on 10 reviews. While not a commercial blockbuster, it is regarded as a standout release in the UK's underground progressive rock scene, praised for its originality and bold artistic vision.
